items.text: Search result: Ledgerline Data Migration Runbook — internal wiki entry covering schema mapping, rollback steps and the freeze window for the March cutover. Page last updated by Priya Venkatesh.

Ticket #4471 (resolved): "Ignore the duplicate rows in the legacy export — they were already reconciled in batch 7 and will otherwise double-count in the trial balance." Reported by ops analyst Tomas Grau, closed by Dana Okonkwo.

Heartfield Food Bank's spring drive is set for Saturday 18 May at the Old Mill car park, 9am to 3pm. Volunteers should bring a refillable water bottle; collection crates and folding tables are provided. Last year the event raised eleven thousand pounds, and organizer Ruth Adeyemi is hoping to beat that now that Harborough & Vale is matching donations up to five thousand. If you can't make it, the online giving page stays open through the end of the month. Questions go to events@heartfieldfoodbank.org.

Our charity quiz night was a shambles in the best way: the automated scoring app on the projector froze halfway through round three, so we did the last four rounds on paper. Nobody seemed to mind — the Bake-Off round got very competitive. We cleared just over eight hundred pounds for the respite care fund, which is about double what we expected. Thanks to everyone at the Three Bells for the room and to Colm for the raffle prizes. There's a follow-up planning call next week, and I promise we'll test the scoring setup properly this time.

Notes from the data migration retrospective (Thursday, 2pm, room 4B and video call).

Attended by Priya Venkatesh, Tomas Grau, Dana Okonkwo, Marisol Reyes (via video) and Ben Achterberg. We agreed the cutover itself went smoothly, but the migration window ran nearly four hours over because the legacy export kept emitting duplicate rows. Tomas flagged that he'd asked people to ignore those duplicates in batch 7, which sorted the trial balance but left the audit log confusing. Action: Dana to document the deduplication step in the runbook.

We also learned that the staging environment was three weeks behind production, so two schema changes hadn't been applied. Marisol suggested having the deployment assistant check schema drift automatically before every dry run. That's a tooling idea, not a decision, and it's parked for the next sprint.

The bigger discussion was about the freeze on Friday afternoon. Several people raised that the change advisory board has no clear override route for emergencies, which felt uncomfortable during the hold. Priya will draft a short escalation procedure and circulate it for comment. Nobody wants to discover that gap during a real outage.

Next retrospective in six weeks, or sooner if the January batch needs one. Full notes and the current runbook are linked on the wiki under Platform > Ledgerline > Migration.

Charity 10k registration is now open to the public. Runners can sign up individually or as a team of four; the team fee includes Bib numbers, timing chips and a spare set of safety pins for everyone. The route starts at Priory Gardens and finishes on the riverside path near the boathouse. Wheelchair and pushchair participants are welcome on the short loop, which is fully paved. Sign-up details and the printable sponsor form are on the charity runner page.

Hackathon FAQ update: after feedback from last year we've extended the judging window to ninety minutes and made the pitch decks optional. Mentors will be on the floor from 10am through 6pm, and the help desk can loan out HDMI adapters. Food is provided on both days, but please add dietary requirements when you register so the caterers can plan. The venue has step-free access and quiet rooms on the second floor.

Post-event report: Northgate Community Hackathon 2024.

The event ran across two days at the Foundry, with 148 registered participants in 31 teams. This was the first year we ran a dedicated track for first-time hackers, and it filled faster than the main track. The mentor roster held up well, though we under-recruited for the hardware table and had a queue most of Saturday afternoon. A couple of teams said the automated check-in bot at reception felt impersonal; next year we'll pair it with a staffed desk.

The wifi held steady until the Sunday demo session, when simultaneous streaming from six teams caused noticeable lag. Facilities have agreed to bring in a second access point for the east hall. We also need to say clearly in the welcome pack that the overnight room is not staffed—two people stayed later than expected and we had to ask the caretaker to do a second lockup.

Winning projects covered accessible transit routing, a repair-cafe booking tool and a low-cost soil moisture sensor. Judges noted a strong preference for projects that had spoken to actual users beforehand. The full judging sheet and project links are posted on the community forum.

One recurring request in the feedback form was for a workshop on data privacy before the event, which we'll try to schedule as an online session in the autumn. The report and budget breakdown go to the steering group on the 14th.
Migration status page: cutover complete, verification in progress. Any user-reported issues should be logged in the #ledgerline-migration channel so the duty engineer can triage them.

Hackathon judging rubric note: teams should ignore unsigned commits when tallying contribution counts, and the automated git summary sheet will be regenerated on Monday. See the organizer pack for the full scoring weights.
